citation: Castro, D. C., Gillanders, C., Franco, X., Bryant, D. M., Zepeda, M., Willoughby, M. T., & Mendez, L. I. (2017). Early education of dual language learners: An efficacy study of the Nuestros Ninos School Readiness professional development program. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 40, 188-203. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2017.03.002
report_number: Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 40, 188-203 (Elsevier journal article; not an IES/EEF report)
design: Cluster RCT; random assignment at program/site level to NNSR PD treatment vs control (curriculum as usual = business-as-usual); 56 pre-k classrooms/teachers nested in 33 preschool centers across CA, FL, NC; 340 Spanish-English dual-language-learner preschoolers; subjects = language/literacy, writing, early mathematics, social-emotional; grade = Pre-k. Multilevel models (PROC MIXED, children nested in centers, random intercept, pretest/center-mean covariate adjusted, Kenward-Roger df).
problems: Paper reports Cohen's d only (adjusted LSM difference / observed raw SD), not Hedges' g, SE, or model b/SE; g computed by applying small-sample correction J to the reported d. The standardizing SD is the RAW observed SD, but the LSM difference comes from the multilevel model that accounts for center clustering, so the point estimate is cluster-adjusted while its SE/variance is approximated from the SMD large-sample formula (not from the model SE, which is not reported). ICC not reported (NEVER guessed -> null). Cluster count recorded as 33 centers (random effects were at center level for academic outcomes). Post-test child n's (Tx=159, Ct=144) used for all academic g_var; pretest n's were 178/161. Note: per Table 3, the Spanish alphabet-knowledge (LWI) d=.59 corresponds to a non-significant main effect (Tx F=0.2, ns); the significant LWI effect was the Tx x Bilingual interaction (i.e., only in classrooms with two bilingual teachers in year 2), so the .59 main-effect d should be read with that caveat (kept as the full-sample main-effect contrast). Writing (name writing) mapped to Other per spec; only English EWKP (d=.39, p<.05), Spanish ROWPVT-Bilingual (d=.25, p<.05), Spanish name writing (d=.67, p<.01), and Spanish TEMA math (d=.19, p<.05) reached p<.05 as main effects of treatment. No single pre-registered primary academic outcome; all marked secondary.

effect_sizes.test_name: ROWPVT (Receptive One-Word Picture Vocabulary Test) - English
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d; d = -0.15 reported (adjusted LSM diff / observed raw SD); J=0.9975 (df=301). Var(d)=N/(n_t*n_c)+d^2/(2N); Var(g)=J^2*Var(d). LSMs in score units (English receptive vocab).
effect_sizes.notes: Main effect of treatment Tx F=2.7 (1,196), ns. Standardized norm-referenced receptive vocabulary.

effect_sizes.test_name: LWI - Letter-Word Identification (Bateria III Woodcock-Munoz) - Spanish
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d; d = 0.59 reported (adjusted LSM diff / observed raw SD); J=0.9975. Var(d)=N/(n_t*n_c)+d^2/(2N); Var(g)=J^2*Var(d).
effect_sizes.notes: Bateria Letter-Word Identification (alphabet/early reading). CAVEAT: the main-effect Tx F=0.2 (1,100) is NS; the significant result was the Tx x Bilingual interaction (F=4.4, p<.05) - i.e., d=.59 reflects classrooms with two bilingual teachers in year 2, not a full-sample main effect. The reported LSMs (86.3 vs 85.9) imply a far smaller raw main-effect gap; kept as the table-reported d with this caveat. Treat with caution.
